udt_error_enum_v0.doc:
Numbered from 100 so the range never overlaps the Stellar Asset Contract's
own codes (1-10). `create_batch` cross-invokes the token, so a caller reading
`Error(Contract, #N)` off a failed Lockup call cannot otherwise tell whose
error it is \xe2\x80\x94 and rendering a token's `BalanceError` as a Lockup schedule
complaint sends the user to fix a field that was never wrong.
udt_error_enum_v0.name: ContractError

function_v0.doc: Withdraws the currently releasable amount to the recipient, on the\nrecipient's own authorization. Partial and repeatable; the cumulative\nwithdrawal can never exceed the amount vested to date.
function_v0.name: claim

function_v0.doc: Refunds exactly the unvested remainder to the sender, on the sender's\nauthorization and only if the Lockup was created cancelable. Everything\nvested at this instant stays claimable by the recipient forever.
function_v0.name: cancel

function_v0.doc:
Pushes the currently releasable amount to the recipient without the
recipient's signature, so a treasurer can drive payouts. Funds can only
ever move to the recipient, so this path grants no extra power over escrow.

Because anyone may call it, a payout must clear `MIN_RELEASE_BPS` of the
deposit \xe2\x80\x94 the floor stops a third party forcing a dust transfer every
ledger, which would bleed the recipient on a token that charges per
transfer. It lifts as soon as nothing more can accrue, so the final
remainder is always sweepable however the Lockup ended, and `claim` never
applies it.
function_v0.name: release

function_v0.doc: Reads a Lockup by id, with its status, vested total, and claimable amount\nresolved at the current ledger timestamp.
function_v0.name: get_lockup

function_v0.doc:
Sets the administrator, whose only power is the creation kill-switch \xe2\x80\x94 it
can never touch escrowed funds, pause claims, or upgrade the contract.

Requiring the admin's own authorization stops an address being named
administrator without its consent. It does not stop a third party
initializing the instance with an address they control before the
deployer gets there \xe2\x80\x94 only a deploy-time constructor closes that, which
the workspace's SDK predates.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc:
Creates one Lockup per (recipient, amount) pair under a shared schedule and
batch id, pulling the total deposit into escrow with a single
`transfer_from` (approve-then-act) and returning the new ids in recipient
order. The service fee moves before the escrow pull; a zero `fee_amount`
skips it.

`batch_ref` is the sender's own name for the batch, which is what lets a
recipient list too large for one transaction land as a single batch: every
call under the same reference joins the batch the first one opened, and
`None` always opens a fresh one. References live in the sender's own
namespace, so one caller can never join another's batch.
function_v0.name: create_batch

function_v0.doc: Returns the amount of a Lockup claimable at the current ledger timestamp.
function_v0.name: get_releasable

function_v0.doc: Returns one page of the Lockup ids belonging to `batch_id`, alongside how\nmany pages exist.
function_v0.name: get_batch_index

function_v0.doc:
Returns one page of the Lockup ids created by `creator`, alongside how many
pages exist. Page 0 is always readable \xe2\x80\x94 an address with no Lockups reports
a page count of 0 and no ids \xe2\x80\x94 and any later page past the count panics
with `PageOutOfRange`. Every paged read below follows the same rule.
function_v0.name: get_creator_index

function_v0.doc: Returns one page of the Lockup ids vesting to `recipient`, alongside how\nmany pages exist.
function_v0.name: get_recipient_index

function_v0.doc: Engages or lifts the creation kill-switch, which blocks `create_batch`\nonly. Claims, releases, and cancellations remain callable in every state.
function_v0.name: set_creation_paused

function_v0.doc:
Hydrates one page of a batch's index into full Lockups. Reading a batch
this way costs pages proportional to the batch, not to the creator's whole
history, which is what keeps a batch addressable for a creator who has made
many.
function_v0.name: get_lockups_by_batch

function_v0.doc: Hydrates one page of a creator's index into full Lockups, carrying the page\ncount so a client walking pages learns where to stop from this same call.
function_v0.name: get_lockups_by_creator

function_v0.doc: Hydrates one page of a recipient's index into full Lockups.
function_v0.name: get_lockups_by_recipient

udt_struct_v0.doc: An escrowed deposit of one token for one recipient, released over a\nsix-scalar schedule. Status is derived from these fields, never stored.
udt_struct_v0.name: Lockup

fields.doc: When the Lockup was canceled, if it ever was. Vesting freezes at this\ninstant. An `Option` rather than a zero sentinel so a cancel can never be\nmistaken for "never canceled", whatever the ledger clock reads.
fields.name: canceled_at

tuple_v0.doc: Page 0 of an address's index, carrying the page count. Held apart from\nthe later pages so an address with few Lockups \xe2\x80\x94 the common case for a\nrecipient \xe2\x80\x94 costs exactly one entry.
tuple_v0.name: Index

tuple_v0.doc: A creator's own name for a batch, mapped to the id this contract gave it.\nKeyed by the creator so one caller's reference can never address another's\nbatch.
tuple_v0.name: BatchRef

udt_struct_v0.doc: The six scalars that describe how a deposit is released. Shared verbatim by\nevery Lockup of a batch.
udt_struct_v0.name: Schedule

fields.doc: Step size in seconds for the streaming portion; 0 or 1 streams per second.
fields.name: granularity

fields.doc: Share of the deposit unlocked at `start`, in basis points. Basis points\nrather than an absolute amount so one schedule fits every recipient of a\nbatch regardless of their individual amounts.
fields.name: start_unlock_bps

udt_struct_v0.doc: One page of an address's Lockup ids, alongside how many pages exist in total\nso a caller learns the range from any single read.
udt_struct_v0.name: IndexPage

udt_struct_v0.doc: A Lockup with the values a caller would otherwise have to recompute, resolved\nat the current ledger timestamp.
udt_struct_v0.name: LockupView

udt_union_v0.doc: Where a Lockup stands at a point in time. Always derived from the Lockup's\nfields, never stored, so it cannot drift from the release math.
udt_union_v0.name: LockupStatus

void_v0.doc: Fully vested, with something still to claim.
void_v0.name: Settled

void_v0.doc: Canceled; the unvested remainder went back to the sender and what had\nvested is still claimable.
void_v0.name: Canceled

void_v0.doc: Nothing is left in escrow \xe2\x80\x94 every unit was withdrawn or refunded.
void_v0.name: Depleted
